problems.table_says: past_tense: dove; past_participle: dived; note: "dove is American; dived is British"
problems.should_be: In American English, both dove and dived are common past-tense forms; dived is not confined to British English. The past participle is usually dived.
problems.reason: The note incorrectly presents dived as exclusively British.

problems.table_says: past_participle: gotten; note: "past participle got in British English"
problems.should_be: Past participles: gotten and got. Got is also common in American English, especially in have got, have got to, and some established senses; gotten is especially American in many other uses.
problems.reason: Got as a past participle is not restricted to British English.

problems.table_says: past_tense: shrank; past_participle: shrunk; note: "also shrunk as past tense; shrunken as an adjective"
problems.should_be: Past tense: shrank or shrunk. Past participle: shrunk or shrunken; shrunken is also widely used adjectivally.
problems.reason: Shrunken is a recognized past-participle form, not merely an adjective.

problems.table_says: comparative: null; superlative: null; note: "comparative with more"
problems.should_be: Comparative: apter or more apt; superlative: aptest or most apt.
problems.reason: Apter and aptest are standard forms, though more apt and most apt are often preferred.

problems.table_says: comparative: null; superlative: null; note: "not gradable"
problems.should_be: Comparative: deader or more dead; superlative: deadest or most dead, depending on sense and style.
problems.reason: Dead is commonly gradable in several senses, for example a deader battery or deader than a doornail.

problems.table_says: comparative: drier; superlative: driest; note: "also dryer, dryest"
problems.should_be: Comparative: drier or dryer; superlative: driest. Dryer is also the usual spelling for the appliance noun; dryest should not be presented as a standard alternative.
problems.reason: Dryest is generally nonstandard; the standard superlative spelling is driest.

problems.table_says: plural: antennas; also: antennae; note: "antennae for the feelers of an insect"
problems.should_be: Plural: antennas or antennae. Antennae is standard for insect feelers and also occurs in technical/scientific uses, including some electronic contexts; antennas is especially common for radio and television structures.
problems.reason: The note unnecessarily and inaccurately restricts antennae to insect feelers.

problems.table_says: plural: media; also: mediums; note: "mediums for people who claim to speak with the dead"
problems.should_be: Plural: media or mediums. Mediums is used not only for spiritualists but also for physical media/materials, sizes, and certain other senses; media is especially common for communication channels and artistic materials.
problems.reason: The stated use of mediums is too narrow.

problems.should_be: Plural: pike for the fish; pikes for weapons and other ordinary count-noun senses.
problems.reason: The invariant plural applies chiefly to the fish sense, not to all senses of pike.
